report:
## Conclusion: The Evidence Is Mixed and Has Shifted Over Time

Your view that probiotics shorten acute infectious diarrhea was supported by the **2010 Cochrane review** (63 trials, 8,014 participants), which found probiotics reduced diarrhea duration by approximately 25 hours and reduced stool frequency, concluding there were "clear beneficial effects" ([Cochrane 2010](https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD003048.pub3/abstract)).

However, the **2020 updated Cochrane review** (Collinson et al., 82 studies, 12,127 participants) **reversed this conclusion**. When the authors focused on large, low-risk-of-bias trials, they found probiotics "probably make little or no difference to the number of people who have diarrhoea lasting 48 hours or longer" and were "uncertain whether probiotics reduce the duration of diarrhoea" ([Cochrane 2020 – PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33295643/?dopt=Abstract); [Cochrane 2020 – Full](https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD003048.pub4/full)). The earlier positive signal was largely driven by smaller, lower-quality studies. As the review's plain-language summary states: "Probiotics may not affect how long acute diarrhoea lasts" ([Cochrane plain-language summary](https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD003048_do-probiotics-help-treat-acute-infectious-diarrhoea)).

Meanwhile, some **newer meta-analyses** (2025–2026) pooling mostly pediatric RCTs still report modest reductions in diarrhea and vomiting duration, though these analyses may include smaller trials and note no significant reduction in hospital length of stay ([Frontiers in Pediatrics 2025](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/pediatrics/articles/10.3389/fped.2025.1722257/full); [Wiley JPN3 2025](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jpn3.70172)).

**Bottom line:** The answer is not a straightforward "yes." The strongest, most recent high-quality evidence (the 2020 Cochrane update) casts significant doubt on whether probiotics meaningfully shorten acute infectious diarrhea, while some meta-analyses of smaller trials still suggest a modest benefit, particularly in children.
